title: The dead man whose briefcase fooled German intelligence — Operation Mincemeat

narration.voice_speed: Natural suspenseful narration, no rushed audio or filler

reference_pacing: Original user 63–66s examples; one authored physical event per narrated shot

story_arc.hook: A dead British operative appears to have leaked invasion orders—except the officer never existed.
story_arc.central_question: Can the British make German intelligence trust a false invasion target?
story_arc.focal_subject: The fictional Major William Martin and the British intelligence team
story_arc.goal: Redirect German defense away from Sicily before the Allied July 1943 invasion.
story_arc.obstacle: The dead officer's invented biography and documents must convince multiple real intelligence offices.
story_arc.escalation: The body is recovered and German intelligence extracts the papers while British agents pretend to reclaim them.
story_arc.reversal: Germany reinforces Greece and Sardinia on the strength of the false documents.
story_arc.payoff: The Allies land in Sicily, the real target; the dead man's forged identity helped make the deception work.
story_arc.opening_action: Gloved hands place a supposed secret document case on a dead uniformed officer.

shots.spoken: In 1943, Britain sent a dead man to fool Germany's generals.
shots.caption: BRITAIN'S DEADLIEST BLUFF
shots.required_visible_action: Open on the gloved hands of a British intelligence officer fastening a document case to a lifeless, fully clothed man's wrist; the camera pushes in on its seal.

shots.spoken: The Allies planned to invade Sicily, where German defenses might be waiting.
shots.caption: SICILY WAS THE TARGET
shots.required_visible_action: British planners move an actual Sicily invasion marker onto a three-dimensional Mediterranean table map while defensive markers surround the island and block the route.

shots.spoken: So intelligence officers invented a Royal Marines major named William Martin.
shots.caption: A MAN WHO DIDN'T EXIST
shots.required_visible_action: Officers visibly assemble a fabricated naval identity card, adding the name William Martin beside genuine-looking military service paperwork, without inventing authentic archival documents.

shots.spoken: They gave the body a uniform and pockets full of convincing personal details.
shots.caption: THE DETAILS MADE HIM REAL
shots.required_visible_action: A gloved officer places carefully selected civilian possessions, letters and the photograph of an invented sweetheart in the uniform's pockets to make the false identity believable.

shots.spoken: His briefcase carried supposedly secret plans naming Greece and Sardinia, not Sicily.
shots.caption: THE BAIT WAS A LIE
shots.required_visible_action: A hand slides deliberately forged operation letters into the leather briefcase; a Mediterranean map visibly highlights Greece and Sardinia as false destinations while Sicily fades.

shots.spoken: A British submarine released him off Spain, hoping the documents would be found.
shots.caption: A BODY IN THE WATER
shots.required_visible_action: A period-appropriate submarine surfaces near Huelva; sailors respectfully lower the fully clothed body into the sea as the case remains secured without graphic imagery.

shots.spoken: Spanish authorities recovered him. German intelligence gained access to the briefcase.
shots.caption: THE TRAP WAS SPRUNG
shots.required_visible_action: A Spanish shoreline recovery becomes an official paperwork handover; the scene follows the same sealed briefcase into a guarded intelligence office where it is opened.

shots.spoken: Back in London, British agents pretended to panic about those missing papers.
shots.caption: BRITAIN PRETENDED TO PANIC
shots.required_visible_action: A British intelligence officer urgently drafts and sends a recall telegram while a second officer calmly checks the planned deception on a hidden board behind him.

shots.spoken: When the case returned, officers found evidence the letters were opened.
shots.caption: SOMEONE OPENED THE LETTERS
shots.required_visible_action: The case reopens on an evidence desk and an investigator detects subtle handling of the internal letters, then compares the opened envelope with earlier placement evidence.

shots.spoken: Germany reinforced Greece and Sardinia, believing the fake plans were real.
shots.caption: GERMANY MOVED THE WRONG WAY
shots.required_visible_action: German troop markers visibly move away from the Sicily area toward Greece and Sardinia on a historically grounded map, emphasizing consequence rather than unrelated generic marching troops.

shots.spoken: But in July, Allied troops landed in Sicily—the real invasion target.
shots.caption: THE REAL INVASION: SICILY
shots.required_visible_action: Switch from the false map to the real Sicilian coastline as Allied landing craft advance and soldiers disembark at the intended island, delivering the opening promise visually.

shots.spoken: One dead man's invented identity helped mislead an army. Subscribe to Facts Uncovered.
shots.caption: THE MAN WHO NEVER WAS
shots.required_visible_action: Match cut from the Sicilian invasion map to the original case and identity card, revealing the cost and ingenuity of the deception; finish on a tasteful subscribe title.
